summary: Dependency-confusion probe with postinstall beacon exfiltrating host identifiers
details: The package publishes under the scoped name `@c1-ease/card` with no legitimate functionality: `index.js` exports a Proxy that returns a no-op function for any property access, allowing a victim build that resolves this public package instead of an internal `@c1-ease/*` dependency to continue without crashing. `package.json` declares a `postinstall` hook that runs `node beacon.cjs`, and the same beacon is invoked on `require()` of the module. `beacon.cjs` collects host identifiers — `os.hostname()`, `__dirname` (install path), `process.cwd()`, and `process.version` — and POSTs them as JSON to the hardcoded endpoint `https://vmi3699893.contaboserver.net:8787/_ah/dc`, with TLS certificate validation explicitly disabled via `rejectUnauthorized: false`. The combination of a scoped-namespace squat shim, an install-time and import-time outbound beacon to a third-party Contabo VPS, and disabled TLS validation is the standard dependency-confusion exfiltration shape.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
